title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, and Comms Templates
author: Marcus Chen
body:
Summary
This playbook defines Redwood Inference’s standard on-call and incident response (IR) process, runbook templates for frequent failure modes, postmortem expectations, rotation/coverage guidance, game day plans, and customer/status‑page communication templates. It is intended for engineers, SREs, support, and product owners who participate in detection, mitigation, and follow-up of service incidents.

Purpose and scope
- Purpose: Reduce time-to-detect, time-to-recover, and customer impact by standardizing roles, escalation paths, and remediation steps.
- Scope: Applies to all production-facing Redwood services (hosted API, Dedicated control plane, Console, private deployment control plane). Non-production outages (dev/staging) should follow the same steps but are not escalated to customer comms unless it affects production.

Key definitions
- Incident: Any event that degrades customer-facing service beyond defined SLOs or causes loss of functionality.
- Severity (sev):
  1) sev-1 (Critical): Wide-impact outage, >50% customers affected, or security incident. Target MTTR: 1 hour.
  2) sev-2 (High): Degraded service (latency/throughput) impacting a significant customer subset. Target MTTR: 4 hours.
  3) sev-3 (Medium): Minor degradation or single-customer impact with workaround. Target MTTR: 24–72 hours.
  4) sev-4 (Low): Non-urgent operational issues, feature regressions without customer impact.

Incident lifecycle (high level)
1) Detection & Triage
   - Alerts, customer reports, or monitoring anomalies are the detection sources.
   - On-call engineer acknowledges in PagerDuty within 5 minutes (SLO).
   - Triage: determine scope, impact, and initial severity using checklists below.
2) Mobilize & Mitigate
   - Assign roles (Incident Commander, Communications Lead, SRE/Service owner).
   - Short-term mitigation to reduce customer impact (fallbacks, rollbacks, route to standby region).
3) Stabilize & Restore
   - Implement fix or coordinated rollback. Validate by metrics and smoke tests.
4) Communicate
   - Internal: Slack incident channel, incident bridge, ops doc.
   - External: status.redwood.ai and customer emails (templates below) for sev-1/2.
5) Post-incident
   - Postmortem within 72 hours for sev-1/2; include timeline, root cause, corrective actions, and owners.

Roles and responsibilities
- Incident Commander (IC): overall decision authority during active incident. Responsible for triage, prioritization, and declaring incident severity.
- Communications Lead: drafts internal and external communications, coordinates with Customer Success.
- Service Owner / On-call SME: provides technical context, executes runbook steps and deploys fixes.
- SRE Lead: ensures platform-level mitigations (scaling, routing, infra).
- Postmortem Author: drafts postmortem and tracks action items to closure.

PagerDuty & escalation policy (summary)
- Primary on-call: 15-minute escalation.
- Secondary: invoked after 15 minutes if primary unresponsive or incident severity escalates.
- Follow-up escalation: On-call manager (30 minutes) then Director of SRE (60 minutes) for ongoing sev-1.

Triage checklist (first 10 minutes)
1) Confirm alert source and validity (monitoring, logs, error-rate spikes).
2) Identify impacted service(s) and customer subsets.
3) Check SLO dashboards: error rate, p95/p99 latency, traffic drop, throughput.
4) Look for recent deploys/rollouts in last 60 minutes.
5) If sev-1/2: notify Communications Lead and open incident channel.

Runbook templates (quick reference)
Note: below are concise, actionable steps. Always record every action in the incident channel and update status page when customer impact is verified.

Runbook: API high p99/p95 latency (hosted inference)
- Symptoms: sustained p99 > 3s and p95 > 1.5s across region for > 5 minutes.
- Immediate checks:
  1) Verify alerts in Datadog and correlate with infra metrics (GPU utilization, queue length, host CPU, network I/O).
  2) Check recent config changes: model routing, batching config, autoscale events.
  3) Confirm whether prefix/KV cache miss rate has increased.
- Mitigation steps (ordered):
  1) If autoscale failed: manually spin up warm instances in affected pool (CLI: infractl scale --pool <pool> --instances +N).
  2) Reduce max batch size or switch to low-latency model variant (temporary routing rule).
  3) Enable degraded mode: disable non-essential pre/post-processing (feature flag: processing.degraded=true).
  4) If issue correlates with a specific model version, route traffic to known-good version.
- Validation: p95/p99 drop back to within SLO for 5 continuous minutes and customer requests succeeding.
- Post-incident actions: add a test to perf-suite, add alert for the root cause metric.

Runbook: GPU node OOM / model OOM on Dedicated pools
- Symptoms: repeated OOM errors, node eviction, worker restarts.
- Immediate checks:
  1) Check node logs, dmesg, kube events.
  2) Verify memory pressure and GPU memory utilization.
  3) Identify if recent model change or quantization profile caused elevated memory.
- Mitigation steps:
  1) Evacuate non-critical pods from affected node to reduce pressure (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets <node>).
  2) Pin inference to nodes with sufficient memory or a lower memory-profile model.
  3) Temporarily reduce concurrency or batch size for affected model.
  4) If persistent, scale up pool with larger instance types and cordon problematic nodes.
- Validation: no new OOM events for 10 min and successful inference logs.

Runbook: Model quality regression (production outputs degrade)
- Symptoms: sudden spike in customer complaints, evals failing, automated quality monitors detect drift.
- Immediate checks:
  1) Pull recent transcripts and evaluation scores.
  2) Check if an A/B rollout or new model push occurred.
- Mitigation steps:
  1) Roll back to previous model version in routing (route rule override).
  2) Disable new model for live traffic and mark it for immediate investigation.
  3) Notify Applied ML / Model Onboarding team to run targeted regression tests.
- Validation: customer complaints decrease and metric baselines return to expected range.

Postmortem process and template
- Requirement: Every sev-1 and sev-2 incident requires a postmortem published within 72 hours. The postmortem must include:
  - Title, severity, incident lead, incident timeline (UTC timestamps), impact summary (customers, duration, SLO breach), root cause, contributing factors, corrective actions (short/long term) with owners and ETA, detection & mitigation timeline, and lessons learned.
- Template checklist:
  1) TL;DR (one paragraph)
  2) Incident timeline (minute-by-minute where possible)
  3) Root cause analysis and evidence
  4) Corrective actions (owner, due date, risk, verification plan)
  5) Customer impact & comms chronology
  6) Postmortem review attendees and approvals
- Postmortem review: Presented at weekly SRE incident review; owners required to update status until actions closed.

On-call rotations and coverage guidelines
- Standard rotation: 2-week primary on-call shifts with 1-week secondary on-call. Primary is responsible for first responder actions and runbook execution.
- Handover: Each on-call should publish a handover note in the oncall channel at shift start/end including known issues, deploys, and planned maintenance.
- Time off & swaps: On-call must be swapped in PagerDuty and Slack updated. No on-call for more than 4 consecutive rotations without manager ok.
- Escalation schedule: documented in PagerDuty with round-robin for primary; contact numbers stored in team vault.

Game days (frequency & objectives)
- Frequency: quarterly platform-wide game days and team-level monthly drills.
- Objectives: validate runbooks, test telemetry & alerting, exercise cross-team comms, and measure MTTA/MTTR.
- Typical game day flow (3 hours):
  1) Pre-brief (15m): goals and injected failure vectors.
  2) Inject incident (15m): synthetic load or simulated node failure.
  3) Active response (60–90m): act as on-call, follow playbook.
  4) Debrief & action items (30m): collect lessons and assign owners.
- Metrics collected: detection time, acknowledgement time, time to mitigation, time to recovery, communication latency.

Status page and customer communications
- Status page policy: all sev-1 and sev-2 incidents must have a public status entry within 30 minutes of incident declaration. Updates should be issued every 30–60 minutes for ongoing incidents until resolved.
- Status page fields: title, start time (UTC), services affected, impact description, mitigation in progress, next update ETA, incident status (investigating / identified / monitoring / resolved).

Customer comms templates (short / adaptable)
- Initial public status (sev-1/2):
  Subject: Redwood Inference — Service Disruption (investigating)
  Body: "We are currently investigating an issue affecting [service / region]. Some customers may experience elevated latency or request failures. Our engineers are actively investigating. We will provide an update by [ETA UTC]. For urgent concerns, contact your account team or support@redwood.ai."
- Update (monitoring):
  Subject: Redwood Inference — Service Update
  Body: "We have implemented a mitigation and are monitoring system behaviour. Some customers may still see intermittent errors while the fix propagates. Next update by [ETA UTC]."
- Resolution notice:
  Subject: Redwood Inference — Incident Resolved
  Body: "The issue affecting [service / region] has been resolved at [time UTC]. We are continuing to monitor and will publish a post-incident report with root cause and actions within 72 hours."
- Template for targeted customer outreach (single customer impacted):
  Subject: Incident affecting your Redwood deployment (ID: [INC-####])
  Body: "Hello [Customer Name],

We experienced a service issue affecting [feature / API]. Your account was [impacted / not impacted]. Our engineers have [mitigated / resolved] the issue at [UTC time]. We will share a post-incident summary with root cause and planned remediations by [date]. If you need immediate assistance, reply to this message or contact your account team.

Apologies for the disruption,
[Account Manager] & Redwood Operations"

Operational tooling and docs
- Incident channel naming: #incident-YYYYMMDD-brief-description (private if security-sensitive).
- Incident runbook checklist: attach runbook, link to dashboards, and paste first-detection logs.
- Logging & evidence: always capture request ids, trace ids, and representative logs for RCA. Store artifacts in the incident folder in the team drive.

KPIs and SLOs to monitor for policy compliance
- Acknowledgement SLO: 90% of alerts acknowledged within 5 minutes.
- Status page SLO: 95% of sev-1/2 incidents with a public status entry within 30 minutes.
- Postmortem SLO: 100% of sev-1/2 postmortems published within 72 hours.

Auditing and continuous improvement
- Monthly incident review: SRE leadership reviews aggregated incidents, recurring causes, and action-item closure rates.
- Runbook hygiene: teams should review and update runbooks after any run (game day or live incident) — mark last-reviewed date in header.

Appendices
A) Quick CLI snippets (examples)
- Scale pool: infractl scale --pool inference-us-east-1 --instances +4
- Route override to previous model: rtrctl set-route --service ml-api --model-version v2025-11-15 --priority 1000
- Drain k8s node: kubectl drain ip-10-0-1-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data

B) Postmortem checklist (publish steps)
1) Create confluence postmortem page using template.
2) Tag SRE, Service Owner, and Product.
3) Link to incident channel, logs, and artifacts.
4) Assign action items with owners and due dates.
5) Present at next incident review and update until closed.

C) Example postmortem TL;DR (for publishing)
- Title: Sev-1 — Hosted API outage affecting p99 latency (2026-01-08)
- Summary: Between 07:12–08:46 UTC, a configuration regression in the batching subsystem increased p99 latency above SLOs for the hosted API. We rolled back the config at 07:34 UTC, which restored baseline performance; full validation completed by 08:46 UTC. Root cause: a new default batch timeout introduced in a canary rollout. Corrective actions: add rollout gating for batching defaults (owner: Platform; due: 2026-02-28), and add automated perf regression tests in CI (owner: Applied ML; due: 2026-03-15).
